sections.content:
Population change in Fareham in 2032

The population in Fareham is projected to decrease from 114,562 people in 2022 to 114,536 people in 2032.

There are seven areas in England where the population is projected to decrease in this period.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 6,181 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Fareham
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Fareham, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 5,090, with 8,327 births and 13,417 deaths in Fareham between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Fareham by 4.4%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 6,181, with 64,583 people moving to the area and 58,402 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Fareham by 5.4%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,196, with 1,629 people moving to the area and 2,824 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Fareham by 1.0%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 248, with 3,535 people moving to the area and 3,287 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Fareham by 0.2%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Fareham in 2032

The median age in Fareham is projected to rise from 47 years in 2022 to 49 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 28% of the population in Fareham are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 24% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Fareham between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Fareham is projected to stay the same, at around 58%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 398 to 453 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Fareham?

In 2032, 17% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 19% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Fareham between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
